mcqs.question: In the reversible reaction 2NO₂(g) ⇌ N₂O₄(g), if the concentration of NO₂ is suddenly increased, what will be the effect on the position of equilibrium according to Le Chatelier’s principle?

options.A: The equilibrium shifts to the left, forming more NO₂
options.B: The equilibrium shifts to the right, forming more N₂O₄
options.C: There is no shift; the system remains unchanged

mcqs.answer: The equilibrium shifts to the right, forming more N₂O₄
mcqs.explanation: Increasing the concentration of a reactant (NO₂) creates a disturbance. Le Chatelier’s principle predicts the system will counteract this by consuming the added NO₂, so the equilibrium shifts to the right, producing more product N₂O₄. Option A is the opposite shift, C ignores the principle, and D is not possible for a reversible reaction.

mcqs.question: For the gas‑phase equilibrium N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) ⇌ 2NH₃(g) at constant temperature, the total pressure is increased by decreasing the volume. In which direction does the equilibrium shift and why?

options.A: To the left, because there are more gas molecules on the left side
options.B: To the right, because the right side has fewer total gas molecules
options.C: No shift occurs; pressure changes do not affect equilibria
options.D: To the side that contains the greater number of moles of gas

mcqs.answer: To the right, because the right side has fewer total gas molecules
mcqs.explanation: Increasing pressure favors the side with fewer moles of gas. The left side has 4 moles (1 N₂ + 3 H₂) while the right side has 2 moles of NH₃. Hence the equilibrium shifts to the right. Option A reverses the logic, C is false for gaseous equilibria, and D is the opposite of the correct principle.

mcqs.question: Consider two equilibria at the same temperature: (i) 2SO₂(g) + O₂(g) ⇌ 2SO₃(g) (exothermic) and (ii) N₂(g) + O₂(g) ⇌ 2NO(g) (endothermic). If the temperature is raised, which statement correctly compares the shift of each equilibrium?

options.A: Both equilibria shift to the right
options.B: Both equilibria shift to the left
options.C: Equilibrium (i) shifts left, while equilibrium (ii) shifts right
options.D: Equilibrium (i) shifts right, while equilibrium (ii) shifts left

mcqs.answer: Equilibrium (i) shifts left, while equilibrium (ii) shifts right
mcqs.explanation: Raising temperature adds heat. For an exothermic reaction (i), heat is a product, so the system counteracts by shifting left (absorbing heat). For an endothermic reaction (ii), heat is a reactant, so the system shifts right to consume the added heat. Options A and B ignore the opposite nature, and D reverses the correct directions.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand effect of catalysts on equilibrium
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about the effect of a catalyst on a chemical equilibrium is correct?

options.A: A catalyst speeds up only the forward reaction
options.B: A catalyst speeds up only the reverse reaction
options.C: A catalyst speeds up both forward and reverse reactions equally, leaving the equilibrium position unchanged
options.D: A catalyst changes the value of the equilibrium constant

mcqs.answer: A catalyst speeds up both forward and reverse reactions equally, leaving the equilibrium position unchanged
mcqs.explanation: A catalyst provides an alternative pathway with lower activation energy for both forward and reverse reactions, so rates of both increase equally. The equilibrium constant, which depends only on thermodynamics, is unaffected. Options A and B are incomplete, and D is incorrect because catalysts do not alter thermodynamic equilibria.

mcqs.question: Le Chatelier’s principle states that when a system at equilibrium is subjected to a change in concentration, pressure, or temperature, the system will respond by:

options.A: Shifting the equilibrium to favor the formation of more products
options.B: Shifting the equilibrium in the direction that counteracts the imposed change
options.C: Remaining unchanged because equilibrium is a fixed state
options.D: Moving toward a state of higher entropy regardless of the change

mcqs.answer: Shifting the equilibrium in the direction that counteracts the imposed change
mcqs.explanation: The principle predicts the system will oppose the disturbance, i.e., shift so as to reduce the effect of the change. Option A is a specific case, not a general rule. Option C contradicts the principle, and D confuses entropy with the specific response to a perturbation.

mcqs.question: In the equilibrium H₂(g) + I₂(g) ⇌ 2HI(g), the concentration of I₂ is decreased. According to Le Chatelier’s principle, the system will:

options.A: Shift to the left to produce more I₂
options.B: Shift to the right to produce more HI
options.C: Show no shift because the change is too small
options.D: Decompose HI equally into H₂ and I₂

mcqs.answer: Shift to the left to produce more I₂
mcqs.explanation: Removing a reactant (I₂) creates a deficit. The system counteracts by shifting toward the left, forming more reactants (I₂ and H₂). Option B describes the opposite shift, C ignores the principle, and D suggests an equal decomposition which is not dictated by Le Chatelier’s principle.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly describes the effect of increasing pressure on a gaseous equilibrium?

options.A: In a homogeneous equilibrium, the shift is always towards the side with fewer gas molecules
options.B: In a heterogeneous equilibrium, pressure changes have no effect because solids and liquids are incompressible
options.C: Both A and B are correct
options.D: Neither A nor B is correct

mcqs.answer: Both A and B are correct
mcqs.explanation: For homogeneous (all‑gas) equilibria, the system shifts toward the side with fewer moles of gas when pressure is increased. In heterogeneous equilibria, only the gaseous components are affected by pressure; solids and liquids do not change volume appreciably, so pressure has little or no effect on the equilibrium position. Hence both statements are true. Options A or B alone are incomplete, and D is false.

mcqs.question: A student observes that the yield of NH₃ in the Haber process decreases when the reactor temperature is increased. Which principle explains this observation and what is the nature of the forward reaction with respect to temperature?

options.A: Le Chatelier’s principle; the forward reaction is exothermic
options.B: Le Chatelier’s principle; the forward reaction is endothermic
options.C: The rate law; the forward reaction is exothermic
options.D: The rate law; the forward reaction is endothermic

mcqs.answer: Le Chatelier’s principle; the forward reaction is exothermic
mcqs.explanation: The synthesis of NH₃ (N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃) releases heat, making it exothermic. Raising temperature adds heat, so according to Le Chatelier’s principle the equilibrium shifts toward the reactants, lowering NH₃ yield. Options B and D misidentify the reaction’s enthalpy, and C confuses kinetic rate considerations with equilibrium shifts.
